successCriteria.description: The LeavePolicy model interface is exported from src/modules/leavePolicy/leavePolicy.model.ts and its status field is typed as the PolicyStatus enum imported from src/shared/types/leave.enums.ts (Phase 1), not a redeclared or string-typed copy.

The repository exposes all four read methods — findAll, findById, findByLeaveTypeId, findActiveByLeaveTypeId — on both the ILeavePolicyRepository interface and the LeavePolicyRepository class that implements it.

findActiveByLeaveTypeId returns only rows whose status is PolicyStatus.ACTIVE for the given leave type id, exercising the composite (leave_type_id, status) access pattern; the other lookup methods return the matching rows or null/empty as appropriate.

The barrel export src/modules/leavePolicy/index.ts re-exports the LeavePolicy interface, the ILeavePolicyRepository interface, and the LeavePolicyRepository class so consumers can import them from the module root.

Jest unit tests in tests/unit/modules/leavePolicy/leavePolicy.repository.test.ts mock the pg Pool and assert each repository method issues the expected query and returns the mocked rows (found case) or null/empty array (not-found case); the suite passes under the existing ts-jest config.

constraints: PolicyStatus must be imported from src/shared/types/leave.enums.ts (Phase 1); the enum must not be redeclared or duplicated in the leavePolicy module.
The repository must receive its pg Pool via constructor injection (matching the LeaveTypeRepository pattern), not by importing the pool singleton from src/shared/db/connection.ts directly.
The module directory and file names must use camelCase (src/modules/leavePolicy/...), matching the existing leaveType module convention rather than the kebab-case used in architecture docs.

This phase is read-only: the repository must expose only the four query methods (findAll, findById, findByLeaveTypeId, findActiveByLeaveTypeId). No create/update/delete/persistence-mutation methods belong in this phase.
outOfScope: LeaveBalance model and repository (Phase 4), LeaveRequest model/repository/service/controller/routes (Phases 5-8), and Fastify app wiring (Phase 8) are out of scope for this phase.
Write/mutation operations on leave policies (create, update, archive, supersede) are out of scope; only read/query methods are specified for this phase.
Database migrations, schema creation, and the leave_policies table DDL are out of scope; the repository assumes the table and its indexes already exist (or is tested against a mocked pool).
HTTP routes, controllers, request validation (Zod), and RBAC/audit enforcement for leave policies are out of scope for this phase — the repository is a data-access layer only.

ambiguities.description: findActiveByLeaveTypeId return cardinality is ambiguous: the composite (leave_type_id, status) index and the Phase 6 service's "validate an active policy exists" usage suggest at most one active policy per leave type, but the schema does not enforce uniqueness on (leave_type_id, status=ACTIVE), so multiple ACTIVE rows could exist. Should the method return a single row (null if none) or an array (empty if none)?
options: Return a single LeavePolicy | null (assume at most one active policy per leave type)
Return an array LeavePolicy[] (allow multiple active policies, caller picks)
Return a single row but order by effective_from DESC and take the first to deterministically pick the latest active policy

entityInvariants.invariant: A LeavePolicy's status is constrained to the PolicyStatus enum values (ACTIVE, INACTIVE, ARCHIVED) imported from the shared enums; the model must not permit any other status value.
effectiveTo is nullable (open-ended policy) but effectiveFrom is always present; a policy with a null effectiveTo is considered currently effective until its status transitions away from ACTIVE.
maxConsecutiveDays is nullable, indicating no upper cap on consecutive leave days for that policy; a non-null value caps the maximum consecutive days allowed.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns all leave policy rows as an array (empty array when none exist); propagates underlying pool query errors without swallowing them.
Returns the single LeavePolicy matching the given id, or null when no row matches; propagates underlying pool query errors.
Returns all LeavePolicy rows associated with the given leave type id as an array (empty array when none match); propagates underlying pool query errors.
Returns the active LeavePolicy row(s) for the given leave type id filtered by status = PolicyStatus.ACTIVE, or null/empty when none match; propagates underlying pool query errors.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The LeavePolicy model must import and use the PolicyStatus enum exactly as defined in the shared enums file (ACTIVE/INACTIVE/ARCHIVED); it must not redefine the enum or use a divergent lifecycle vocabulary.

The LeavePolicyRepository must follow the same structural pattern as LeaveTypeRepository: a constructor-injected pg Pool, an interface (ILeavePolicyRepository) paired with an implementing class, single-row lookups returning result.rows[0] ?? null, and list lookups returning result.rows.
The leavePolicy barrel export must mirror the leaveType barrel: re-export the model interface and the repository interface/class from the module root.

The repository unit tests must follow the established test pattern: jest.mock('pg') with a mock Pool exposing a mock query function, mockResolvedValueOnce for rows, and toHaveBeenCalledWith assertions on the SQL and params, covering both found and not-found cases per method.

integrationPoints.why: The LeavePolicy model imports PolicyStatus from the shared enums; this is the hard dependency declared by the phase.
The repository operates against the pg Pool type; in production the Pool instance is sourced from the shared db connection, though the repository itself receives it via constructor injection.

Phase 6 (LeaveRequest service) depends on ILeavePolicyRepository.findActiveByLeaveTypeId to validate that an active policy exists for a leave type before creating a leave request; this phase establishes that contract.
